## About me

I'm a PhD student and biologist in the laboratory of Dr. Rachel Green in the Johns Hopkins University Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics. I'm broadly interested in how cells sense and respond to translational distress. Specifically, I'm interested in how this occurs at the level of the ribosome via the ribotoxic stress response and the integrated stress response. Through this work, I have developed deep expertise in molecular biology and bioinformatics, particularly in mammalian cell culture systems.

Prior to this, I worked as a protein biochemist at the Broad Institute's Center for the Development of Therapeutics (CDoT). There I purified and characterized candidate proteins to support fragment-based screening and structural biology efforts as a part of multiple drug discovery campaigns. This experience further honed my skills acquired from Dr. Jason Young's group at McGill University. My Bachelor's and Master's theses utilized biochemical and biophysical techniques to characterize proteins involved in the heat shock response *in vitro*.

I am almost entirely self-taught in programming after learning about its utility during my last year of undergrad. I have significant experience in Python, R, and bash scripting, which has been incredibly helpful during my graduate work.
